item.title: Most tweens and teens use AI for schoolwork and emotional support, a new survey shows
item.description: Four out of five teens are using AI chatbots for schoolwork and emotional support, according to new survey data.

item.title: Becca Freeman examines ambition and long-lost love in new book 'Back Where We Started'
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with author Becca Freeman about her new romance Back Where We Started, about returning home and reuniting with someone left behind.

item.title: Civil rights leader Dolores Huerta has died at 96
item.description: Iconic civil rights leader, Dolores Huerta, has died. She was 96 years old. In the 1960s, Huerta co-founded, with Cesar Chavez, the Mexican-American union that would become the United Farm Workers.

item.title: Fans are not happy that WNBA finals game 6 will be played during work hours
item.description: Fans are enraged that Game 6 of the WNBA finals will be played in the middle of the day Thursday to make room for a routine NBA game.

item.title: Deadlock in Israeli elections means weeks of political jockeying
item.description: With no clear winner in Israeli elections, the opposition has to decide if it allies with Arab parties.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
item.description: The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.

item.title: Colombia's government sparks backlash with museum art purge
item.description: Colombia's new president vows a "cultural counterrevolution" against wokeness, and his removal of 47 artworks from a national museum is sparking protests and fears of government censorship.

item.title: Polls close in Israel with opposition ahead but no clear winner
item.description: Voting in Israel has ended and exit polls suggest most Israelis have voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But the center-right opposition may struggle to build a governing coalition.

item.title: Hotel owner in the Andes organizes his community to watch for fires
item.description: In the Peruvian Andes, a hotel owner is helping his community prepare for wildfires. It's a role that's put him and other local businesses at the forefront of helping Peru respond to El Nino threats.

item.title: For Milwaukee Brewers 1st baseman Jake Bauers, this World Series is extra special
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers almost didn't play in this World Series. In 2024, he came close to quitting baseball to become a stay-at-home dad. But he needed health benefits.
